choices.text: Hold back the storm one evening so the copyist can finish her page

effects.log: The sky stays grey and still. She finishes, caps her ink, and goes home dry.

choices.text: Keep the thanks, and turn it over in the Pale Gallery

effects.log: It is the lightest thing in the room. You keep it.

choices.text: Ask in a dream what she would change

effects.log: She says: no thunder during copying. You agree.

events.text: A prayer reaches you from a copyist who has never believed in gods. "If you are there, I do not need you to do anything. I only wanted to say it out loud, to someone." It is the most honest prayer you have heard in a century.

choices.text: Answer nothing and listen in the Pale Gallery's hush

effects.log: You listen the whole hour. They feel it and sleep easily.

choices.text: Send a quiet sign: a ripple in the ink

effects.log: The ink in her cup ripples once. She looks at it a long time.

choices.text: Ask your pantheon what this is called

effects.log: They have no word. You name it.

events.text: A mother prays that her child's bad eye might ease, and the prayer is wrong in an instructive way: she asks the wrong god, for the wrong thing, and misspells your name. It reaches you anyway, because the love in it knows the way. You stay with the wrongness of the address.

choices.text: Ease the bad eye yourself and leave no mark

effects.log: She thanks the wrong god. The child sees well.

choices.text: Forward the prayer to the god of Healing with a copyist's note

effects.log: He answers dryly. The mother gets a remedy.

choices.text: Learn from how love finds the address through a thousand temples

effects.log: You trace the route. It is a map.

events.text: You have been a god for so long that boredom has started to show, a pale grey patch at the edge of everything. Nothing is wrong. It is only that the colours you used to chase are the colours you are now made of. A small child's drawing on your altar is the only bright thing in a century.

choices.text: Study the drawing for a year

effects.log: You study it. It is bright because it is not trying. That is a Dao of its own.

choices.text: Find a new, small thing to love

effects.log: You choose something silly: a particular kind of moss. It saves the age.

choices.text: Accept the boredom as a texture

effects.log: You accept it. It turns out to be a kind of contentment with the lights off.

events.text: The last mortal who remembers your first name is very old and has begun to forget. They sit in a garden and say it softly, again and again, like a spell. When they die, the name will be yours alone. You find you are not ready to be the only one who knows it.

choices.text: Visit in a dream and say it with them

effects.log: You say it together. They go to sleep on the last syllable, and it is a blessing.

choices.text: Tell your name to a young god

effects.log: You tell it. They do not understand the gift, and that is part of the gift.

choices.text: Write the name on the first page of a book

effects.log: You write it. A book remembers things for people who forgot to.

events.text: Two pantheons ask you to arbitrate a quarrel about a star that both of them claim. You are known to be fair, which means you are known to be tired. They each send a delegation with gifts. You can hear the gifts clinking.

choices.text: Judge fairly, and refuse the gifts

effects.log: You return the gifts. The ruling holds because it is not for sale.

choices.text: Propose the star be shared by turns

effects.log: You propose a rotation. Neither is pleased and both abide.

choices.text: Recuse yourself; your fairness is worn thin

effects.log: You decline. The quarrel finds another judge, and you rest.

events.text: A throne has been offered to you: a seat at the head of a pantheon. It carries a Dao of its own, a gravity that would pull yours into orbit. You examine it for a season. The throne is made of the stuff of the Dao you have spent your whole life preserving.

choices.text: Decline the throne

effects.log: You decline. The pantheon is hurt and impressed, and a year later grateful.

choices.text: Accept for one age only

effects.log: You accept, with an end date written on the arm. It is a strange way to rule, and a good one.

choices.text: Accept, and rule as lightly as you can

effects.log: You accept. You do very little and the realm flourishes, and everyone asks how.

events.text: A god of your pantheon, tired past telling, asks you for a way to retire. There is none; gods do not retire, they only dim. But they want, very simply, to sit in a garden and not be asked for anything. You have the standing to make it so.

choices.text: Make them a garden no prayer can reach

effects.log: You make it, a pocket of quiet in the domain of your own. They sit in it, content, for a thousand years.

choices.text: Ask the pantheon to give them a long sabbatical

effects.log: The pantheon grumbles and grants it. A new custom is born.

choices.text: Sit with them in the garden yourself

effects.log: You sit. It is the best week you have had since the Upper Realm.

events.text: The foundation under you is still settling. Twelve thousand years is the old measure for this rung, and you feel it in the hollow behind your eyes: not a pain, a patience. Below the clouds a calendar turns over a whole age without noticing you sat still.

choices.text: Lie still like the seam of rock and let weight settle

effects.log: You let the world rest on you the way a hill rests on its seam. The hollow behind your eyes fills with slow grey calm.

choices.text: Sit by the midwife in the lying-in room through one long night

effects.log: You watch a birth from the corner and understand that settling is what comes after the hard hour.

events.text: A flaw you had forgotten is setting into your foundation along with everything else: a habit of thought from a rung ago, now twelve thousand years from being moved. Saengmo says it can still be turned if you take it up now, or built into the wall if you do not.

choices.text: Tend it like a child that never grew

effects.log: You hold it, feed it, and let it grow up. By the end it is a trait and no longer a fault.

choices.text: Ask the midwife what a long labour teaches about patience

effects.log: She says you do not pull the thing out. You stop pulling, and the habit loosens by itself.

events.text: You wake from a three-year meditation with Saengmo's lamp burning at the foot of your seat. They kept it lit the whole time and left a note: the foundation was loud in the night, and they did not want you to wake in the dark.

choices.text: Plant a seed in the lamp-oil dish as thanks

effects.log: A sprout comes up by morning, lit gold at the tip. Saengmo looks at it and says nothing, and is moved.

choices.text: Ask the midwife why mothers keep a lamp lit for the first week

effects.log: She says it is for the one being born, who is afraid. You see yourself in that and say so.

events.text: The gate above you is shut, and the reason is plain: it asks for a second Dao at Mastery, and you do not have it yet. You stand before it every few centuries, as one stands before a locked door in one's own house, and know there is nobody to shout at.

choices.text: Wake the second Dao at Mastery by feeding it plain work

effects.log: You give it small tasks each day. It learns to bear weight, one hour at a time.

choices.text: Learn bearing from the midwife's steady hands

effects.log: She lets you hold a breath beside hers through a long labour. You come out of the room knowing what mastery bears.

events.text: Saengmo is certain your Dao is deep enough for what is next. The gate disagrees, and the gate has read it more carefully than anyone. It asks for a second Dao at Mastery, and a friend's confidence is not on the list.

choices.text: Tell Saengmo that faith is a seed and the gate is a season

effects.log: Saengmo laughs, and says a seed does not mind either. You are both comforted.

choices.text: Be sharp with the gate and let it hear about it

effects.log: You say what you think of the gate to its face. It is not hurt. You are, a little, by the echo.

events.text: A mortal scholar's prayer asks why a god cannot simply walk through a gate they are strong enough for. You read it twice. The honest answer is that the gate asks for a second Dao at Mastery, not strength, and you are still turning the difference over.

choices.text: Answer with a seed and a small instruction to plant it

effects.log: The scholar plants it, and a plant takes the whole year to open, and so does the answer.

choices.text: Ask the midwife to tell the scholar why babies do not walk at birth

effects.log: She does, kindly, over broth. The scholar writes it down and stops asking.

events.text: Saengmo tells you, over tea nobody drinks, about the time the gate above this rung turned them back. They went in sure and came out with their sleeves smoking. The lesson was a small one, they say, and took four hundred years to understand.

choices.text: Ask Saengmo what grew from the failure

effects.log: Saengmo says a small mushroom, in the shape of a door. They show you where, and you eat it.

choices.text: Ask what they would plant for the next one

effects.log: They say nothing: let the ground be fallow a season. You leave the ground fallow.

events.text: You hear that a god one rung above you tried the gate after it and failed. The Silent Hall will not say how. A candle is lit for them in a temple older than the town that holds it, and the whole pantheon is careful not to look at the candle.

choices.text: Plant something beside the candle

effects.log: A sprout comes up in the night. Nobody will say who planted it.

choices.text: Ask the midwife what she says to someone who lost the baby

effects.log: She says: "You were there." You say it to the candle.

events.text: You find a record in the Hall of old ascents: a god's account of their own failure at this gate, written for no one. The last page says they stopped trying and simply taught for a thousand years. It reads as if it were the best outcome they could imagine.

choices.text: Seek the old teacher and sit in the back of their school

effects.log: The school is a field of small plants. You are given a pot and a lesson.

choices.text: Copy out the last page and press a leaf in it

effects.log: The leaf stays green for a thousand years. It becomes a small proof that endings can be soft.

events.text: The night before you try the gate, the world is odd. The seeds in the bowl lean toward you. Your foundation is the shape of a held breath. You wonder, for the first time in ages, what you would regret not having said to someone.

choices.text: Plant the regret in a pot and water it

effects.log: Overnight a shoot comes up, small and green. You take it to the gate as a companion.

choices.text: Sit with the midwife at a bedside and say nothing till dawn

effects.log: A child is born at the hour you meant to try the gate. You hold its first breath in your own.

events.text: On the eve of the gate, Saengmo appears at your door with a sealed jar and no explanation. The jar holds an old breeze. "For afterwards," they say, "if you want to remember what it was like to be only this."

choices.text: Take the jar and set it beside a seedling

effects.log: The seedling grows toward it. You water both.

choices.text: Open it near the lying-in room and let a child have it

effects.log: A newborn breathes it and sneezes. The midwife says it is a good sign.

events.text: A tally of the twelve thousand years behind you is the oddest comfort. You list what you learned at each rung, and notice that the best things were not what you were chasing. Tomorrow you try the gate. Tonight you finish the list.

choices.text: Press the list into the earth and plant something over it

effects.log: A tree comes of it, small, and a good shade tree. You never learn the species.

choices.text: Read it to the midwife as one reads to the newly born

effects.log: She hums along. You are, for an hour, a child being told a story.

events.text: Saengmo taps a place behind your knee and says there is a hairline in the foundation there. Not a danger, but a place where weather will one day find a way in. It sits in the exact spot where you were proudest.

choices.text: Graft a living thing over the hairline

effects.log: A thread of green takes root across the crack. It is weaker than stone and stronger than a wound.

choices.text: Let the crack teach you where pride grows thin

effects.log: You study the places in you that bruise easily. There are fewer than you feared.

events.text: A hollow in your divine foundation shows up only on feast days, when the faithful of a lying-in room press too close. Your power swells and a little of you thins at the edges, like paper held to a lamp. You do not quite recognize your own voice at the end of the day.

choices.text: Have the faithful bring seeds instead of prayers

effects.log: The pressure becomes a gentle patter of small hopes. You thin less.

choices.text: Let the midwife sit by you during the rites as an anchor

effects.log: She holds your wrist like a pulse. The hollow cannot open under that hand.

events.text: You found a flaw in the way you hold your Dao: it leans toward a world's tides, and away from the small things that live in it. A divine foundation can tilt for ten thousand years without cracking, and be wrong the whole time.

choices.text: Apprentice for a season with the midwife

effects.log: You learn to hold a hand, boil water, and say nothing. Small work, big lesson.

choices.text: Count the heartbeats in a room of sleepers

effects.log: There are eleven. Your Dao stops leaning away from the very small.

events.text: You can feel a world of voices at once in the cool quiet of your work: not as sound, but as pressure, like deep water. Today a prayer comes up through it that is more tender than most, and your qi leaps in answer before you have chosen to hear.

choices.text: Answer with a small sign of life at their window

effects.log: A seed sprouts in a chipped pot. They stare. The qi in you is bright and soft.

choices.text: Let it ripple through you to a mother who needs it

effects.log: It lands on a bedside, and the midwife feels it. You are lighter.

events.text: A famine has driven everyone around a lying-in room to your name, and the prayers are the loudest you have ever heard. Faith like that is a rare strength. It is also the strength of people who have nothing left to spend, and you know what it costs them.

choices.text: Take a little and answer with a green flush on the fallow fields

effects.log: Shoots appear on the margins. Little, but sufficient to carry them through.

choices.text: Refuse the strength and send the midwife's wisdom of gruel and water

effects.log: You fill them with sense in a dream. It does more than power would.

events.text: The faithful have taught you by accident. The prayer of a midwife, long and dull and sincere, moves your qi more than a dazzling one. It is the repetition that does it, like a sea against a rock, and you have been waiting for lightning when you should have loved the tide.

choices.text: Listen to the midwife's daily thanks for one safe birth

effects.log: It is the same every day, and it moves you like new rain.

choices.text: Share the finding with the Green Assembly

effects.log: They laugh, and plant a bed of it. The Assembly is wiser by a leaf.

events.text: Your people have built you a temple older than the town that holds it. They hang offerings on its rail every dawn, not grand ones: a swaddling cloth, a child's drawing of you with too many arms. The offerings do something for your qi, and something else for your temper.

choices.text: Hold the swaddling cloth against the child you will never meet

effects.log: You warm it gently. A mother wraps her baby in it that night.

choices.text: Receive the offerings, and plant the cut flower

effects.log: It takes root beside the old temple. The wall grows green by spring.

events.text: The keeper of a temple older than the town that holds it has quietly become rich on your name, and the offerings now go through three hands before they reach the altar. You can feel the thinning in your qi. The priest is old, kind to their neighbours and, you think, afraid.

choices.text: Show the priest his own children in a dream

effects.log: He wakes with a start. The offerings reach the altar by noon.

choices.text: Send a young midwife to serve the temple honestly

effects.log: She changes the place in a year. The priest is shamed into kindness.

events.text: On your festival day, at a temple older than the town that holds it, a family of strangers leaves no offering at all. They simply sit on the steps and eat, and talk, and let a child nap with her head on a worn stone. Your qi rises more from that than from the heaped altar.

choices.text: Let the old temple's stones warm for the child

effects.log: The worn stone holds the heat of centuries. The child sleeps deep.

choices.text: Ask the wardens to leave a blanket and say nothing

effects.log: They do. The mother puts it over her child in her sleep.

events.text: Your domain stretches now across a world's tides, and a small thing in it happens only because you let it: a late frost holds off, a river changes its mind. You are discovering that a god's power is mostly a list of things they decline to do.

choices.text: Decline one more ripening, and watch a bud wait

effects.log: It waits. The late flower is the finest of the year.

choices.text: Reach for a small act: bring one stalled birth on gently

effects.log: It comes, mother and child well. Your power feels like a held breath let go.

events.text: Two of your domain's laws have begun to disagree. The same rain that feeds a field drowns a village below it, and you are the only one who can say which matters more. Saengmo has offered to hold one of the laws for you while you think.

choices.text: Accept Saengmo's offer to hold the law of growth, and think a hundred years

effects.log: They hold it in an open palm. You think. The answer grows slowly into view.

choices.text: Decide at once for the field, and bear what follows

effects.log: You choose and the village below dries. You send them a well.

events.text: A god of the silent hall asks to see how you keep your domain. They stay a month, taking notes, asking questions, never praising. On the last day they say your domain is the least beautiful they have seen, and the most alive.

choices.text: Thank them for the honest note

effects.log: They are pleased and a little rattled. Seeds of ideas travel home with them.

choices.text: Ask what they would change in your First Seeds

effects.log: They name three things. You change two, and keep the one that blooms.

events.text: A Revelation arrives over a lying-in room the way weather arrives: not as words, but a rearrangement of the air. You spend a month deciphering it and are left with one phrase you cannot stop turning over, like a stone in the mouth. It seems to be about patience.

choices.text: Plant the phrase and let it sprout

effects.log: A word comes up as a shoot. You water it carefully.

choices.text: Share it with the midwife's circle and hear their guesses

effects.log: They guess seven meanings. Three are better than yours.

events.text: A manual of the gods has come into your keeping, copied seven times over by seven tired hands. In the margin of the fourth chapter, someone has written in a different ink: "This does not work near a seam of rock." You are not sure if that is a warning or a joke.

choices.text: Try the chapter beside a seam of rock and see what holds

effects.log: The rock holds. The chapter does not. The note was half right.

choices.text: Look for the note's author among the old midwives

effects.log: One of them was a scribe once. Her notes are in a cradle.

events.text: In the night a Revelation comes that is not for you. It is meant for a young god of Life, and has simply fallen on the wrong roof, here beside a lying-in room. It is lovely, and it will do you a little good, and it is not yours.

choices.text: Plant it in the soil of the young god of Life's garden while they sleep

effects.log: They wake to find it blooming. They thank the garden.

choices.text: Read it to a newborn first, then pass it on late with fruit

effects.log: The child sleeps through it. You apologise with a basket.

events.text: A clerk of the Heavenly Court asks you to confirm a line in the Book of Fates: a midwife is to die in their sleep, tonight, at forty. It is a small, ordinary line. You are not required to object. The ink is not quite dry.

choices.text: Confirm it, and send a safe birth into the next house

effects.log: You sign, and the line closes. A child is born down the lane an hour later, easily.

choices.text: Ask the clerk for a day, and sit with her midwifery students

effects.log: You read their notes. She taught well, and the line stands without a hole in it.

events.text: You are called as a witness before a Judge of Souls. A midwife you once answered with a small mercy stands accused of selling short measure at a lying-in room. Your testimony will not decide, but it will weigh. The Judge asks nothing but "What did you see?" and waits.

choices.text: Tell exactly what you saw in the lying-in room

effects.log: You describe the pan, the water, the measure given. The Judge sees the measure was fair.

choices.text: Ask the midwife to be called as a character witness

effects.log: She is. The matter ends before noon.

events.text: The Court's archivist gives you a rare gift: an hour alone with the Book of Fates, open at your own page. It is blank except for a single line in a small neat hand: "Waiting on you." You find that this is the most comforting sentence you have read.

choices.text: Close the Book and plant the line in a pot

effects.log: It grows, a shoot with no leaf. You keep it by the window.

choices.text: Write a line, and read it to the midwife

effects.log: She says it sounds like a good name. You rub it out.

events.text: You spend a century with a seam of rock, the nearest thing to what your Dao answers: you let it slip through your fingers, you taste it, you let it carry you. You discover that the Dao is not the element, but the way the element refuses to be held.

choices.text: Press your palm against a seam of rock until you feel its refusal

effects.log: It does not give, and does not hurt. You learn mass by what it will not grant.

choices.text: Hold a stone gently and put it down without a sound

effects.log: You learn to hold and set down. The rock stays itself.

events.text: You have watched a seam of rock a million times, and today it looks different. It is nothing. It is the same element at a new angle. Your Dao takes a half-step and you are very careful not to move.

choices.text: Hold still while the seam of rock shifts its face

effects.log: A new grain shows. The step finishes with a small hush.

choices.text: Follow the new angle into the rock

effects.log: You follow the seam to a hollow with a fossil. You bring back a shell.

events.text: A child at a lying-in room is playing with a seam of rock, not knowing it. They are doing it badly and joyfully, and a thing you spent a thousand years learning falls out of their hands by accident. You are not sure whether to be annoyed.

choices.text: Watch the child tap the rock and listen for what answers

effects.log: She hears a hollow in the stone you had missed. You steal the hollow.

choices.text: Send a dream of a patient quarryman to show her a good pry-bar

effects.log: She grows up to move stone with a finger. She never knows why.

events.text: You are asked to give the opening address at a council of pantheons in the Hall of First Seeds: a short talk on what a god owes the faithful. The Will of Heaven says order, the Silent Hall says remembrance, the Green Assembly says growth, the Throne of Storms says weight. You must pick, or find a fifth.

choices.text: Say a god owes room to grow, and open the doors of the First Seeds

effects.log: The Green Assembly rises. Vines enter, and the Hall is full of the smell of earth.

choices.text: Say a god owes the faithful a safe beginning

effects.log: The Silent Hall inclines; the midwife in the gallery laughs aloud.

events.text: A doctrine you have followed for ages turns out, on a close reading, to be a mistranslation: one word (bear) was swapped by a scribe, and an entire school of devotion built on the swap. The error is beautiful. Correcting it would cost a lot of people their favourite prayer.

choices.text: Publish the correction, with a seed in each copy

effects.log: Every copy goes out with a seed. The reformation is greener than expected.

choices.text: Add a footnote that the old word may be read as a lullaby

effects.log: It becomes a lullaby. The mistake becomes a song.

events.text: In the Hall of First Seeds, a god of the Silent Hall asks you to explain your doctrine without using any of its words. You try and fail. You try again and succeed halfway. By the end you have learned what you actually believe, which is smaller and truer than the doctrine.

choices.text: Thank them and rewrite your teaching as a garden

effects.log: You plant it instead of writing it. Half your students leave; the rest tend it.

choices.text: Admit that the doctrine is a seed and a seed is not the tree

effects.log: They smile; a sprout lifts in the hall.

events.text: You catch yourself at the old etiquette again: carrying a fan you never open. It is a habit from your Upper Realm centuries, and the gods in the Hall of First Seeds are politely baffled. A cup is just a cup here.

choices.text: Open the fan in the middle of the Hall of Seeds and fan the seedlings

effects.log: They lean toward the breeze. The Hall is delighted.

choices.text: Keep the unopened fan; it is yours

effects.log: The Green Assembly adopts a fan with a seed in it.

events.text: You still keep a ledger of favours owed, a leftover of the immortals' exchange. The oldest line is a healed child. A god would never keep one, and when a friend sees it they look briefly hurt. The ledger is accurate to the grain, and entirely beside the point.

choices.text: Plant the ledger's pages in a pot and see what sprouts

effects.log: Something green comes up. You do not know the species.

choices.text: Keep it, but write beside each line the name of a child you helped

effects.log: The ledger becomes a register of births.

events.text: You flinched at a raised voice today. The Upper Realm taught you to expect a hand behind such things, and the habit lives in the shoulders long after the cause is gone. Here nothing is behind them, and your body has not yet been told.

choices.text: Stay in the lying-in room when a voice is raised, and breathe

effects.log: The voice is only a voice. Your shoulders drop.

choices.text: Ask the midwife how she keeps her hands steady in a loud room

effects.log: She says: she hums. You hum with her.

events.text: A midwife prays, in a lying-in room, with a newborn's blanket in their other hand. They do not ask for anything. They only say "thank you for the weather." You, who keep weather, find that nobody has ever thanked you for it before.

choices.text: Warm the lying-in room by a degree for the midwife and the mother

effects.log: Both breathe easier. The midwife thinks it was her own doing.

choices.text: Keep the thanks in the seam of a rock

effects.log: It rings faintly for a long time.

events.text: A prayer reaches you from a midwife who has never believed in gods. "If you are there, I do not need you to do anything. I only wanted to say it out loud, to someone." It is the most honest prayer you have heard in a century.

choices.text: Answer nothing and sit with her by the bedside

effects.log: You sit the whole hour in the corner. They sleep easily.

choices.text: Send a quiet sign: a seed rolling to rest beside her hand

effects.log: She looks at it a long time and does not ask.

events.text: A mother prays that her child's weak breath might ease, and the prayer is wrong in an instructive way: she asks the wrong god, for the wrong thing, and misspells your name. It reaches you anyway, because the love in it knows the way. You stay with the wrongness of the address.

choices.text: Ease the weak breath yourself and leave a sprig of mint

effects.log: She thanks the wrong god. The child breathes.

choices.text: Forward the prayer to the god of Healing with a midwife's note

effects.log: He answers gruffly. The mother gets a remedy.

events.text: The foundation under you is still settling. Fifteen thousand years is the old measure for this rung, and you feel it in your whole shadow, which has stopped following: not a pain, a patience. Below the clouds a calendar turns over a whole age without noticing you sat still.

choices.text: Let your stopped shadow lie where it fell

effects.log: You stop calling it back. It lies on the floor of the colonnade, and the foundation stops being afraid of being alone.

choices.text: Go to the foundry and watch a bell cool

effects.log: The bell-founder lets the casting cool unmoved for a day. Settling, you see, is only cooling with company.

choices.text: Follow the rising tide a day up the shore

effects.log: You walk with the tide and let it carry the weight. When it turns you turn with it.

choices.text: Ask Haeryong how long a sea waits to be full

effects.log: Haeryong says it never is, and that is the good of it. You sleep that night as if you had been told a secret.

events.text: A flaw you had forgotten is setting into your foundation along with everything else: a habit of thought from a rung ago, now fifteen thousand years from being moved. Haeryong says it can still be turned if you take it up now, or built into the wall if you do not.

choices.text: Cast it into a bell and listen to its true note

effects.log: The bell-founder pours it in with the bronze. The flaw rings one clear tone that you can finally hear.

choices.text: Let the tide wear it smooth over a year of walking the shore

effects.log: It takes the tide a thousand turns. Afterward the flaw has no edges, only a shape.

choices.text: Ask Haeryong whether the Sea ever fixes its own flaws

effects.log: Haeryong says it only moves them to another coast. You laugh, and take the hint.

choices.text: Build it into the wall of the Drowned Colonnade as a keystone

effects.log: You bury it where it carries weight. It holds the arch and never speaks again.

events.text: You wake from a three-year meditation with Haeryong's lamp burning at the foot of your seat. They kept it lit the whole time and left a note: the foundation was loud in the night, and they did not want you to wake in the dark.

choices.text: Hang a small bell by Haeryong's door

effects.log: It rings once when the tide changes. Haeryong understands, and rings back.

choices.text: Carry the lamp down to the tideline and light the shore

effects.log: Fishers come down the beach, see the little light, and sit. By dawn there is a fire and soup.

choices.text: Keep the note and the lamp, and let them burn together

effects.log: You set both on the colonnade ledge and watch. Paper curls, oil holds, and neither is wasted.

choices.text: Say nothing until the tide has turned twice

effects.log: You wait two tides before you speak. By then you know what to say, and it is short.

events.text: The gate above you is shut, and the reason is plain: it asks for both of your Daos perfected, and you do not have it yet. You stand before it every few centuries, as one stands before a locked door in one's own house, and know there is nobody to shout at.

choices.text: Perfect the lesser Dao first, in the foundry

effects.log: You hammer the lesser Dao on the bell-founder's anvil until it rings true. The gate hears the bell.

choices.text: Ask the tide how a sea is both its waves and its depth

effects.log: The tide answers by coming in. You take the lesson in two halves, wave and depth.

choices.text: Rest the first Dao for a decade while the second catches up

effects.log: You hold the first still and tend the second. The gate is neither moved nor insulted.

choices.text: Share the work with Haeryong, who has been where you are

effects.log: Haeryong lends you a season of their attention. It is the rarest loan.

events.text: Haeryong is certain your Dao is deep enough for what is next. The gate disagrees, and the gate has read it more carefully than anyone. It asks for both of your Daos perfected, and a friend's confidence is not on the list.

choices.text: Ask Haeryong to be honest about what they see

effects.log: Haeryong says your second Dao is half a tide short of full. It is exact, and you are grateful.

choices.text: Let the bell-founder cast a gate-bell with your faults in the bronze

effects.log: She casts it and hangs it in the foundry. Every time it rings, you remember.

choices.text: Thank them, and carry the gate's answer to them gently

effects.log: You tell your friend plainly what the gate wants. They do not argue, and go quiet, and stay.

choices.text: Try the gate once more, tired, and be turned

effects.log: It does not open. You walk home along the Colonnade at low tide, and sleep.

events.text: A mortal scholar's prayer asks why a god cannot simply walk through a gate they are strong enough for. You read it twice. The honest answer is that the gate asks for both of your Daos perfected, not strength, and you are still turning the difference over.

choices.text: Answer in the sound of a bell being cast

effects.log: The scholar hears it in a dream: a molten bell cooling slowly. They wake knowing what a key is made of.

choices.text: Keep the prayer near the tideline and let the sea answer it too

effects.log: The tide leaves the answer in sand, one line at a time. You copy it down.

choices.text: Send the scholar a ship with an old captain who knows the harbour bar

effects.log: The captain tells them nothing but the bar, and the scholar understands the gate.

choices.text: Answer plainly and sign it with your real name

effects.log: The scholar goes still. You have never signed one before, and now you may have to again.

events.text: Haeryong tells you, over tea nobody drinks, about the time the gate above this rung turned them back. They went in sure and came out with their sleeves smoking. The lesson was a small one, they say, and took four hundred years to understand.

choices.text: Ask Haeryong what the sea thinks of the gate

effects.log: Haeryong says the sea thinks nothing of gates. You go home feeling the gate is smaller than it was.

choices.text: Ask them to describe the tide in the hour they were turned

effects.log: They describe it exactly. You hear in it the wrong coin and the right one.

choices.text: Say you will go at the turn of the tide, not before

effects.log: Haeryong nods like a harbour master. You will wait, then, and that is half the lesson.

choices.text: Say you will bring the bell-founder as a witness

effects.log: Haeryong laughs, and says to bring a bell, not a witness.

events.text: You hear that a god one rung above you tried the gate after it and failed. The Silent Hall will not say how. A candle is lit for them in a bare room where the whole sky is the congregation, and the whole pantheon is careful not to look at the candle.

choices.text: Row out and cast a bell into the water where the god was last seen

effects.log: The bell sinks with a long low note. A year later a fisher hauls it up and rings it.

choices.text: Study what the tide left of the attempt

effects.log: Scraps of a Dao wash up along the Colonnade. You read them, one by one, as warnings.

choices.text: Sit with the candle and let the whole shrine be quiet

effects.log: No one speaks. The tide turns while you sit.

choices.text: Carry the failed god's unfinished work forward a small way

effects.log: You pick up one thread of it and do that much. It is a modest memorial and a real one.

events.text: You find a record in the Hall of old ascents: a god's account of their own failure at this gate, written for no one. The last page says they stopped trying and simply taught for a thousand years. It reads as if it were the best outcome they could imagine.

choices.text: Copy the page and cast it into a bell

effects.log: The bell-founder pours the words into the bronze. It rings the last page on the hour.

choices.text: Seek the god and ask what it was like to stop

effects.log: They say it was like putting down a very heavy hammer. They hand you one and say try it.

choices.text: Read it on the shore at low tide and let the sea answer

effects.log: The sea says nothing. You stay until it has said it all.

choices.text: Put it back and go on, but loosen your grip

effects.log: You loosen it a hair. It is enough to feel the difference.

events.text: The night before you try the gate, the world is odd. The tide stands still for a breath. Your foundation is the shape of a held breath. You wonder, for the first time in ages, what you would regret not having said to someone.

choices.text: Say it to the tide and wait for it to turn

effects.log: The tide stands still for a breath, then goes out with your sentence. You sleep as it goes.

choices.text: Let the bell-founder cast a small bell for it

effects.log: She pours it by lamplight. In the morning you have a bell that rings only your sentence.

choices.text: Walk the Drowned Colonnade in your shadow-less quiet

effects.log: No shadow follows you. You find you do not mind, and arrive at dawn with a light step.

choices.text: Write it on the wall of the colonnade and leave it for the sea

effects.log: The sea writes over it by noon. You will never know who reads it.

events.text: On the eve of the gate, Haeryong appears at your door with a sealed jar and no explanation. The jar holds an old breeze. "For afterwards," they say, "if you want to remember what it was like to be only this."

choices.text: Take the jar and cast its stopper into the tide

effects.log: The stopper floats. The jar stays corked. You cannot tell which is the gift.

choices.text: Open it on the shore and let it join the tide-wind

effects.log: The old breeze flows out to sea. A wave comes in that is warmer than it should be.

choices.text: Ask the bell-founder to seal it in a small bell

effects.log: She does. The bell is silent till you strike it, and then it plays a morning.

choices.text: Refuse and keep your gaze on the water

effects.log: Haeryong takes it without comment. You wonder at your own sternness.

events.text: A tally of the fifteen thousand years behind you is the oddest comfort. You list what you learned at each rung, and notice that the best things were not what you were chasing. Tomorrow you try the gate. Tonight you finish the list.

choices.text: Read it to the tide and let it take the pages

effects.log: The tide takes them one at a time. The sea is now a little more literate.

choices.text: Cast the list into bronze as a bell-inscription

effects.log: The bell-founder pours it. Each year is a ring around its shoulder.

choices.text: Give the list to a young god of the Sea

effects.log: They are fifteen hundred years old and read it with their feet in the water. They cry a little, happily.

choices.text: Keep the list and add one more year before you go up

effects.log: You write: tomorrow. It looks wrong and right.

events.text: Haeryong taps a place at the root of your tongue and says there is a hairline in the foundation there. Not a danger, but a place where weather will one day find a way in. It sits in the exact spot where you were proudest.

choices.text: Let the tide fill the hairline and call it a harbour

effects.log: The sea settles in it. You are proud of the harbour, which is a better kind of pride.

choices.text: Cast a thin bronze patch over it

effects.log: The bell-founder's metal holds. The seam rings when you tap it, and you grow fond of the sound.

choices.text: Ask Haeryong how many cracks the sea has

effects.log: Haeryong says none, since all of it is cracks. You find this oddly comforting.

choices.text: Seal it, and dedicate the sealing to someone you wronged

effects.log: It takes the whole decade. At the end you are lighter than the crack.

events.text: A hollow in your divine foundation shows up only on feast days, when the faithful of a foundry press too close. Your power swells and a little of you thins at the edges, like paper held to a lamp. You do not quite recognize your own voice at the end of the day.

choices.text: Hold the feast on the tide-flat at ebb

effects.log: The crowd is wide, the sea is far, and nothing presses. You are whole by dusk.

choices.text: Let the bell-founder ring the closing hour on a cast bell

effects.log: The bell ends the rite on a note that gathers you back together.

choices.text: Let the crowd thin you, and follow your own edges back in

effects.log: You walk yourself home along the shape of the thinning. It is a surprisingly tidy road.

choices.text: Ask Haeryong how the sea manages to be so many places

effects.log: Haeryong says it does not manage, it simply gives up edges. It is the wrong advice, and you tell them so kindly.

events.text: You found a flaw in the way you hold your Dao: it leans toward the turn of an age, and away from the small things that live in it. A divine foundation can tilt for ten thousand years without cracking, and be wrong the whole time.

choices.text: Spend a season mending one net with a bell-founder's patient wife

effects.log: You mend it badly and then well. The lean corrects itself in your fingers.

choices.text: Listen to the smallest wave on every shore

effects.log: You hear one, then a thousand. The tide has its own small things.

choices.text: Ask a child of the foundry what the biggest thing is

effects.log: The child says: the pot. You go and look at the pot.

choices.text: Study the lean as a tide, and let it turn

effects.log: You do not correct it. It reverses in its own time, and with it your understanding.

events.text: You can feel more prayers than there are stars to carry them in the cool quiet of your work: not as sound, but as pressure, like deep water. Today a prayer comes up through it that is more tender than most, and your qi leaps in answer before you have chosen to hear.

choices.text: Answer with a quiet tide that lifts a boat

effects.log: The boat rises; the sailor looks up. You take a measure of strength with gratitude.

choices.text: Let the prayer ride the current on to a farther coast

effects.log: It reaches someone who needed it more. You feel no loss, only distance.

choices.text: Take it into the foundry and temper it

effects.log: The bell-founder's heat lets it settle as strength. You say a thank-you.

choices.text: Ask Haeryong how a sea hears every prayer without drowning

effects.log: Haeryong says: by being many small hears. You try it.

events.text: A famine has driven everyone around a foundry to your name, and the prayers are the loudest you have ever heard. Faith like that is a rare strength. It is also the strength of people who have nothing left to spend, and you know what it costs them.

choices.text: Take a little and answer with a run of fish up the estuary

effects.log: The nets come up heavy. The tide has paid off, and the strength is spent well.

choices.text: Refuse the strength and turn a fleet from another sea

effects.log: You call it with a tide-song. The fleet comes in, laden, and sets down at the quay.

choices.text: Drink it fully; this is the age of the sea

effects.log: You swell, and your tide swells with you. You feel the hunger turn in the waves.

choices.text: Ask the bell-founder to cast a bell that rings when hunger rings

effects.log: The bell is hung on the quay. When it tolls, the village shares bread.

events.text: The faithful have taught you by accident. The prayer of a bell-founder, long and dull and sincere, moves your qi more than a dazzling one. It is the repetition that does it, like a sea against a rock, and you have been waiting for lightning when you should have loved the tide.

choices.text: Listen to the bell-founder's mutter over each casting

effects.log: It is the same few words every time. The tide in it is a long, slow gift.

choices.text: Teach the colonnade to hear what is dull

effects.log: You hold a class. The students are bored, and then they are not.

choices.text: Count how many dull prayers make one swell

effects.log: It takes four hundred. You write the number on the wall.

choices.text: Keep it as a private craft

effects.log: You keep the knack to yourself. It deepens, and so does the quiet around you.

events.text: Your people have built you a bare room where the whole sky is the congregation. They hang offerings on its rail every dawn, not grand ones: a small bell, a child's drawing of you with too many arms. The offerings do something for your qi, and something else for your temper.

choices.text: Ring the small bell they hung, once, in thanks

effects.log: It is the smallest sound on the whole shore. A child hears it and laughs.

choices.text: Receive the offerings and say nothing for an age

effects.log: You let the tide of gifts rise. It is a quiet, heavy kind of qi.

choices.text: Ask the priests to give the gifts to the shore's poor

effects.log: They do. The rail is bare and the shore is warm.

choices.text: Hang a small offering of your own on the rail

effects.log: You hang a thread of seaweed. The priests don't know what to make of it.

events.text: The keeper of a bare room where the whole sky is the congregation has quietly become rich on your name, and the offerings now go through three hands before they reach the altar. You can feel the thinning in your qi. The priest is old, kind to their neighbours and, you think, afraid.

choices.text: Send the bell-founder a dream of an empty bell

effects.log: She casts a bell with no clapper and gives it to the priest. He understands.

choices.text: Let a storm come and strip the false from the gifts

effects.log: It lifts every gold leaf off the altar. The priest sits on the steps and weeps.

choices.text: Send the shore's children to sing in the temple every dawn

effects.log: He cannot take the money while they sing. In a month the books are straight.

choices.text: Mind the thin tide of qi and say nothing

effects.log: It is a smaller sea than before. You keep your counsel and wonder if that is wisdom.

events.text: On your festival day, at a bare room where the whole sky is the congregation, a family of strangers leaves no offering at all. They simply sit on the steps and eat, and talk, and let a child nap with her head on a worn stone. Your qi rises more from that than from the heaped altar.

choices.text: Hold back the weather from the bare room

effects.log: The whole sky is their roof. It stays clear till they leave.

choices.text: Ask the wardens to let a few children join them

effects.log: Three more come. The steps become a picnic.

choices.text: Study what a congregation of one family does to a whole sky

effects.log: It is the smallest congregation and the widest prayer. You note it.

choices.text: Quietly turn the tide of stars to keep the child's sleep unbroken

effects.log: The constellations arrange themselves gently. Nobody sees the fuss.

events.text: Your domain stretches now across the turn of an age, and a small thing in it happens only because you let it: a late frost holds off, a river changes its mind. You are discovering that a god's power is mostly a list of things they decline to do.

choices.text: Decline one more flood, and log it on the Colonnade wall

effects.log: The wall gains a mark. A long-dreaded tide goes by without taking a field.

choices.text: Reach for a small act: turn a single tide an hour early

effects.log: It turns, and a stranded boat is free. The sea notices and does not mind.

choices.text: Walk the turn of the age and ask what is owed

effects.log: The age answers in tide-tables. The sum surprises you.

choices.text: Ask Haeryong what they decline most often

effects.log: Haeryong says: the second wave. You write it down.

events.text: Two of your domain's laws have begun to disagree. The same rain that feeds a field drowns a village below it, and you are the only one who can say which matters more. Haeryong has offered to hold one of the laws for you while you think.

choices.text: Accept Haeryong's offer to hold the law of the tide, and think a hundred years

effects.log: They hold the tide like a heavy bell. You think. The answer comes with the next spring.

choices.text: Decide at once, and attend the moved people's weddings

effects.log: You choose. The coast is redrawn; you dance at every wedding on the new shore.

choices.text: Give the law to the shore-folk and the bell-founder to decide

effects.log: They hold a council over a ship's bell. The answer is a sea-wall with a gate.

choices.text: Split the law in two and hold half each with Haeryong

effects.log: It holds. You and Haeryong become, for a while, a single weather.

events.text: A god of the green assembly asks to see how you keep your domain. They stay a month, taking notes, asking questions, never praising. On the last day they say your domain is the least beautiful they have seen, and the most alive.

choices.text: Thank them; the compliment is exact

effects.log: They go home with notes on tides they will never see. You call it a good trade.

choices.text: Ask what they would change in the Colonnade

effects.log: They name three things. You change two, and the one that hurts is the one that drowns.

choices.text: Return the visit and take notes in turn

effects.log: You spend a month in the Throne of Storms being unpraised. Rain pelts the inkwell.

choices.text: Ask them to stay and write the second half of the survey

effects.log: They stay a season. The survey is the first true map of your sea.

events.text: A Revelation arrives over a foundry the way weather arrives: not as words, but a rearrangement of the air. You spend a month deciphering it and are left with one phrase you cannot stop turning over, like a stone in the mouth. It seems to be about patience.

choices.text: Cast the phrase into a bell and listen to it ring

effects.log: The bell speaks. The phrase becomes a sentence you understand for an hour.

choices.text: Read it to the tide and see what it returns

effects.log: The tide returns one wave, and the wave means yes. That is enough.

choices.text: Share it with the colonnade scribes

effects.log: They quarrel brilliantly. A note on tides goes into the library.

choices.text: Keep it, and ask no more of it

effects.log: You file it away in a drawer of sea-grass. It hums.

events.text: A manual of the gods has come into your keeping, copied seven times over by seven tired hands. In the margin of the fourth chapter, someone has written in a different ink: "This does not work near a rising tide." You are not sure if that is a warning or a joke.

choices.text: Try the chapter at the turning of the tide, and watch it fail twice

effects.log: The second failure is the instructive one.

choices.text: Ask the bell-founder whether she knows the hand

effects.log: She does. It belongs to a man who cast a bell for a god that fell.

choices.text: Write beside it: "Try it underwater"

effects.log: It sits in the library for a thousand years. One day a diver tries it.

choices.text: Copy the chapter out again without the note

effects.log: It is a clean text. It is also worse.

events.text: In the night a Revelation comes that is not for you. It is meant for a young god of the Sea, and has simply fallen on the wrong roof, here beside a foundry. It is lovely, and it will do you a little good, and it is not yours.

choices.text: Float it on the tide to the young god of the Sea it was meant for

effects.log: It floats into their arms. They believe it a gift of the water itself.

choices.text: Cast a bell around it and deliver the bell

effects.log: The bell-founder makes a hollow bell. It rings the Revelation to the one who strikes it.

choices.text: Ask Haeryong to carry it, since the Sea carries everything

effects.log: Haeryong does, and says nothing. You are secretly relieved.

choices.text: Keep it

effects.log: It does you good. You take a long walk along the Colonnade at low tide.

events.text: A clerk of the Heavenly Court asks you to confirm a line in the Book of Fates: a bell-founder is to die in their sleep, tonight, at forty. It is a small, ordinary line. You are not required to object. The ink is not quite dry.

choices.text: Confirm it, and toll the foundry bell in her name

effects.log: The bell rings for the bell-founder's death an hour early, on a lucky day for the foundry.

choices.text: Ask for a day, and watch the tide go out and come in once

effects.log: You see the whole sea take a day to breathe. You sign at dusk.

choices.text: Decline to confirm, and send the sea to carry him home gently

effects.log: The Book frowns. The sea wins. He wakes in the morning at sea, unharmed, unremarked.

choices.text: Ask whether the death could be an apprenticeship instead

effects.log: The clerk checks. It cannot. You write a note that it should.

events.text: You are called as a witness before a Judge of Souls. A bell-founder you once answered with a small mercy stands accused of selling short measure at a foundry. Your testimony will not decide, but it will weigh. The Judge asks nothing but "What did you see?" and waits.

choices.text: Tell exactly what you saw at the foundry

effects.log: You describe the bronze, the weight, the day. The Judge writes it all.

choices.text: Ask the tide to be brought in as evidence

effects.log: The Judge looks bemused and allows a bucket of seawater. It does not help, but it is dramatic.

choices.text: Tell it kindly, and a little more

effects.log: You stretch the day by one tide. The Judge watches you do it.

choices.text: Decline: you do not weigh bronze against a bell

effects.log: The Judge accepts it. You walk home along the Colonnade, a little emptier.

events.text: The Court's archivist gives you a rare gift: an hour alone with the Book of Fates, open at your own page. It is blank except for a single line in a small neat hand: "Do not hurry." You find that this is the most comforting sentence you have read.

choices.text: Close the Book and cast the line into a bell that has never been struck

effects.log: The bell is unstruck and the line unwritten. You keep both.

choices.text: Write a line, and let the tide have the page

effects.log: The tide takes it. You are relieved and a little jealous.

choices.text: Ask the archivist whether the sea writes anything

effects.log: The archivist says: once a year, on a beach no one visits. You go look.

choices.text: Sit with the line a full tide, saying nothing

effects.log: It makes no demand. The tide comes and goes. You rise comforted.

events.text: You spend a century with a rising tide, the nearest thing to what your Dao answers: you let it slip through your fingers, you taste it, you let it carry you. You discover that the Dao is not the element, but the way the element refuses to be held.

choices.text: Stand knee-deep as the tide rises and let it take back the sand

effects.log: It undoes your footing, again and again. You learn the tide by losing ground.

choices.text: Cup a handful of the rising tide and let it find its own level

effects.log: It returns to the sea in your palm. You hold, you let go, you are warmer.

choices.text: Ask the tide what it thinks it is for

effects.log: It answers in the long low note of a bell. You carry it ages.

choices.text: Stay a hundred years where the tide turns

effects.log: The turning point is as small as an eyelid. You are patient there.

events.text: You have watched a rising tide a million times, and today it looks different. It is nothing. It is the same element at a new angle. Your Dao takes a half-step and you are very careful not to move.

choices.text: Hold still while the tide shows a new face

effects.log: It runs a new line up the sand. The step finishes with a hush.

choices.text: Follow the new angle out to sea

effects.log: You follow it to a bar of sand that was never there. You bring back a pebble.

choices.text: Write it down for the colonnade library

effects.log: The librarians read it and shelve it under Tides, Minor. It is later reclassified.

choices.text: Ask the bell-founder whether metal ever does this

effects.log: She says: once, at the pour. She shows you the bell.

events.text: A child at a foundry is playing with a rising tide, not knowing it. They are doing it badly and joyfully, and a thing you spent a thousand years learning falls out of their hands by accident. You are not sure whether to be annoyed.

choices.text: Watch the child float a bowl in the tide-pool

effects.log: The bowl sails nowhere with great authority. You steal the authority.

choices.text: Send a sea-wind to carry her bowl one lap of the pool

effects.log: It sails, and she cheers. She never knows who helped.

choices.text: Keep away; tide-pools are for the young

effects.log: You leave her to it. She names a crab.

choices.text: Ask the bell-founder to let the child strike a small bell

effects.log: She does. The child rings it three times and is a bell-founder in her mind.

events.text: You are asked to give the opening address at a council of pantheons in the Drowned Colonnade: a short talk on what a god owes the faithful. The Will of Heaven says order, the Silent Hall says remembrance, the Green Assembly says growth, the Throne of Storms says weight. You must pick, or find a fifth.

choices.text: Say a god owes the age its turning, and have the Colonnade tide rise to your ankles

effects.log: The water laps the hall. The Throne of Storms is delighted and wet.

choices.text: Say a god owes the faithful a place for their dead at sea

effects.log: The Silent Hall inclines; Haeryong sends a wave to say yes.

choices.text: Say a god owes patience in a hurry

effects.log: The Will of Heaven winces. The Green Assembly laughs approvingly.

choices.text: Propose a fifth: a god owes the tide to turn

effects.log: The council debates it for a tide. The fifth is carried by a single wave.

events.text: A doctrine you have followed for ages turns out, on a close reading, to be a mistranslation: one word (turn) was swapped by a scribe, and an entire school of devotion built on the swap. The error is beautiful. Correcting it would cost a lot of people their favourite prayer.

choices.text: Publish the correction with the turning of the tide

effects.log: The old word goes out with the ebb; the new one comes in with the flow.

choices.text: Footnote it, and cast the footnote into a bell

effects.log: The bell rings both readings in turn. It is oddly harmonious.

choices.text: Ask the sea-faithful which word they sing, and follow them

effects.log: They sing the old one and mean the new. You leave it alone.

choices.text: Keep it quiet; the tide has used it for ages

effects.log: You say nothing. You walk the shore at night, uneasy.

events.text: In the Drowned Colonnade, a god of the Green Assembly asks you to explain your doctrine without using any of its words. You try and fail. You try again and succeed halfway. By the end you have learned what you actually believe, which is smaller and truer than the doctrine.

choices.text: Thank them and rewrite your teaching as a tide-table

effects.log: It lists what rises and what falls. Half your students leave; the rest read the sea.

choices.text: Admit that the doctrine is a tide and a tide is not the sea

effects.log: They smile; the Colonnade floods to the ankles.

choices.text: Defend the doctrine out of habit

effects.log: You defend it with grace. The visitor nods and goes. The water in the hall drains.

choices.text: Teach it to the bell-founder without words and see if it takes

effects.log: She hums it into bronze. It takes, in a different key.

events.text: You catch yourself at the old etiquette again: speaking only after the second cup. It is a habit from your Upper Realm centuries, and the gods in the Drowned Colonnade are politely baffled. A cup is just a cup here.

choices.text: Speak before the second cup, once, and see who notices

effects.log: Nobody notices. The Colonnade tide carries the sentence out.

choices.text: Keep the second-cup rule; let it be a quirk of the age

effects.log: Two pantheons adopt a version. It becomes a custom with a bell.

choices.text: Ask Haeryong why the Sea waits for the second cup

effects.log: They say it waits for the tide, which is rude of it. You laugh.

choices.text: Pour the second cup into the sea

effects.log: It goes where all cups go. The sea says nothing and approves.

events.text: You still keep a ledger of favours owed, a leftover of the immortals' exchange. The oldest line is a bell cast. A god would never keep one, and when a friend sees it they look briefly hurt. The ledger is accurate to the grain, and entirely beside the point.

choices.text: Cast the ledger into the sea page by page

effects.log: The tide takes them. You are poorer and more at ease.

choices.text: Keep the ledger but let a bell be cast from its ink-weight

effects.log: The bell is a small sweet-voiced thing. It rings when someone owes you nothing.

choices.text: Update the ledger with what you owe the sea

effects.log: The sum is humbling and cold.

choices.text: Ask the bell-founder what a cast bell is owed

effects.log: She says: to be rung. You ring one.

events.text: You flinched at a rising tide today. The Upper Realm taught you to expect a hand behind such things, and the habit lives in the shoulders long after the cause is gone. Here nothing is behind them, and your body has not yet been told.

choices.text: Wade into the surf at its loudest and keep still

effects.log: It comes, it goes. Your shoulders drop.

choices.text: Swim out past the breakers to where it is quiet

effects.log: It is quiet there. You float.

choices.text: Ask a god born in the sea how they learned not to flinch

effects.log: They were never taught. You envy them an hour.

choices.text: Strike the foundry bell and let it ring through you

effects.log: It does. By the end you are loose.

events.text: A bell-founder prays, in a foundry, with a hammer in their other hand. They do not ask for anything. They only say "thank you for the weather." You, who keep weather, find that nobody has ever thanked you for it before.

choices.text: Hold the wind off the foundry yard so the bell-founder's pour is clean

effects.log: The bronze runs without a bubble. He pats the hammer and says nothing, grinning.

choices.text: Keep the thanks inside a bell and let it ring for others

effects.log: It rings a long low thank-you. Fishers hear it as luck.

choices.text: Ask in a dream what he would change

effects.log: He says: nothing, but a drier Thursday. You see to it.

choices.text: Stop the tide for a breath, so he can finish his pour in peace

effects.log: It stands, then goes. Nobody but you and he know.

events.text: A prayer reaches you from a bell-founder who has never believed in gods. "If you are there, I do not need you to do anything. I only wanted to say it out loud, to someone." It is the most honest prayer you have heard in a century.

choices.text: Answer nothing and let the tide whisper until they sleep

effects.log: It whispers low. They sleep easily.

choices.text: Send a quiet sign: a single bell-note over the water

effects.log: They hear it and do not ask why.

choices.text: Ask your pantheon what this is called

effects.log: They have no word. You name it after a bell.

choices.text: Ask Haeryong whether the Sea has ever been prayed to like this

effects.log: They say: constantly, by everyone, and nobody knows. You are humbled.

events.text: A mother prays that her child's sleepless night might ease, and the prayer is wrong in an instructive way: she asks the wrong god, for the wrong thing, and misspells your name. It reaches you anyway, because the love in it knows the way. You stay with the wrongness of the address.

choices.text: Ease the sleepless night yourself and send the tide to hush the shore

effects.log: She thanks the wrong god. The child sleeps.

choices.text: Forward the prayer to the god of Healing with a bell attached

effects.log: He grumbles, and the bell rings. The mother gets a remedy.

choices.text: Learn from how love finds the address through a rolling sea

effects.log: You follow it as a boat follows a bell. It is a map.

choices.text: Answer in the wrong god's voice, deliberately

effects.log: It is the strangest favour you have done. She weeps with thanks.

events.text: There is no foundation left to settle. What remains is the holding: a Dao kept in one place while everything that has a name tries, gently, to wear it down. You catch yourself leaning on it, and straighten.

choices.text: Hold it without leaning

effects.log: You let go of the leaning and find the Dao stands on its own. That is the whole art of this rung, and it takes a thousand years to learn.

choices.text: Lean on it a little, honestly

effects.log: You admit that a Dao held for this long is also a companion. The leaning does not break it. It is only a kind of thanks.

choices.text: Ask a peer how they hold theirs

effects.log: They laugh kindly and say they do not know either. It is the most useful answer anyone has given you in a century.

events.text: A very old habit has begun to show in how you hold the Dao: a flinch from when you were small enough to fear things. It is not a flaw, quite. It is the last place in you that a thing could still happen to.

choices.text: Keep the flinch

effects.log: You decide it is the one door you will leave unlocked. The Dao holds just as well, and you stay a little more alive.

choices.text: Smooth it out

effects.log: The flinch goes, and so does something that made you listen. You are steadier and a little further from everyone.

choices.text: Show it to someone you trust

effects.log: You show a peer, and they show you theirs. Nobody speaks for a while.

events.text: A new god has asked you how long it takes to be finished. You gave the honest answer, which is that you are not, and watched them decide whether to be disappointed. They are very young. They have been a god for four hundred years.

choices.text: Tell them the part that is good

effects.log: You tell them about the quiet that comes when the climbing stops. They go away thoughtful, which is all you wanted.

choices.text: Tell them nothing more

effects.log: You let them keep the question. Some answers are only any use if the asker earns them.

choices.text: Ask what they thought finished would be like

effects.log: Their answer is a small, bright picture of a throne. You do not correct it. You only ask who they thought would be sitting on it.

events.text: There is no gate above you. For the first time in a hundred thousand years nothing is shut against you, and you do not know where to put your attention. The Dao keeps its seat under you, quietly, like a dog glad to be home.

choices.text: Look back down the stairs you came by

effects.log: You look down at every gate you stood before. Each one looks smaller, and each one was exactly the right size.

choices.text: Rest your attention on the Dao itself

effects.log: You turn to the thing you have carried so long and look at it, plainly, as if for the first time. It looks back.

choices.text: Go and find where the others are stuck

effects.log: You carry the news down to the lower gods that the stairs end. Some are comforted and some are furious.

events.text: A very young god asks you what is above this rung. You say nothing, and they hear that as a secret. By evening there are three rumours of a seventh heaven, and two of them agree on its colour.

choices.text: Correct the rumour gently

effects.log: You say there is no heaven above this one, and that it is enough. The rumour dims, and a few go home easier.

choices.text: Let it grow a little

effects.log: A mystery is a way to keep the young climbing a while longer. You wonder if it is kind, and let it stand.

choices.text: Tell them the true shape of the top

effects.log: It is a place you hold, not a place you reach. They nod as if they understood and certainly do not.

events.text: You are asked, in the Hall of Records, what you would do if the Dao in your hands were taken away. The question is meant as a trap or a kindness; you cannot tell. You find you have an answer, and it is not an answer you expected to have.

choices.text: Say you would sit down and rest

effects.log: The hall is silent a moment, and then someone laughs. It is the best sound you have heard in a century.

choices.text: Say you would learn another

effects.log: You say a Dao is a way of walking, and you would learn another. Three gods write it down.

choices.text: Decline to answer

effects.log: You say the question is for another day. It follows you home, and sleeps on the step.

events.text: A peer lost their hold on one of their two Daos last year. It did not break; it only slipped, as a hand slips on a rope. They come to you in the cold hour and ask, without any pride, how it is that yours stays.

choices.text: Tell them the truth, which is that you do not know

effects.log: You say you grip it and then forget you are gripping. They go away and try forgetting. It is not an answer, but it is a door.

choices.text: Sit with them while they hold it again

effects.log: You sit beside them through a year of their holding. It is not a cure, and it is the thing they needed.

choices.text: Show them how you rest the Dao on the ground

effects.log: You show them how to put it down and pick it up. It frightens them, and then it helps.

events.text: A decision of yours, long settled, turns out to have been wrong. Not wicked, only wrong: a domain went slowly dry because you kept it in a way that suited you. Nobody has noticed but a river in a country you have never visited.

choices.text: Go and put it right

effects.log: You go to the river and put it right. It takes a century and you do not ask for thanks.

choices.text: Tell the pantheon what you found

effects.log: You tell them. The silence is long and a little admiring, and one god asks if they might check their own.

choices.text: Quietly fix it and say nothing

effects.log: It is done by the next flood. You tell yourself it is the same as honesty, and are not sure.

events.text: At the foot of your seat, a small thing has been cracking for ages: a custom you made for your domain that has outlived its use. You can feel it from here, like a bad tooth. To pull it will hurt a few thousand people who love it.

choices.text: Pull it, and mourn it with them

effects.log: You pull it with a hundred gods and a hundred thousand mortals at the funeral of a custom. Afterward it feels like a spring.

choices.text: Leave it and let it fade

effects.log: You leave it. It fades in its own time, a slow kindness, and nobody is angry at you.

choices.text: Replace it with a better custom

effects.log: You write a new one and make it easy to love. The old one is only missed a little.

events.text: A turning of the age is near; you can feel it in the way old prayers begin to sound unfamiliar. The gods who rule the turning will ask you to hold the line while it comes. Tonight you walk the whole of your domain, as if to say goodbye to how it is.

choices.text: Walk it slowly and take your time

effects.log: You walk the domain from edge to edge. Each place greets you in its own way, and none of them knows you are saying goodbye.

choices.text: Walk it quickly and check the joints

effects.log: You tighten every seam you can find. By dawn the domain is ready for weather it has never met.

choices.text: Do not walk it, and trust what you built

effects.log: You stay where you are and trust. It is a harder walk than the other kind.

events.text: Before a great working, Mujin appears with a sealed jar and no explanation. It holds an old breeze. "If it goes badly," they say, "open it, and remember what it was like to be only a person."

choices.text: Take it and keep it close

effects.log: You put the jar in your sleeve. It sits against your arm like a small, steady creature.

choices.text: Open it now and let it blow free

effects.log: The breeze goes out through the roof. You feel it join a wind somewhere over a sea you once crossed.

choices.text: Ask them to keep it for you

effects.log: They agree, and neither of you says what it means. It is a very old kind of trust.

events.text: You are asked to speak at the turning of an age. You have nothing prepared. You stand before a hall of a thousand gods and a billion unseen mortals, and understand that what they want is not wisdom. It is a voice they can lean on while it passes.

choices.text: Speak plainly and briefly

effects.log: You say three sentences. The hall is quiet for a long time after, and somebody weeps with relief.

choices.text: Say you do not know what is coming

effects.log: The honesty lands harder than comfort would have. Several gods thank you, privately, for not lying.

choices.text: Tell an old story

effects.log: You tell the story of the first lamp. By the end they are all remembering something of their own.

events.text: Mujin taps a place between your shoulders and says there is a hairline in the foundation there. Not a danger, but a place where weather will one day find a way in. It sits in the exact spot where you were proudest.

choices.text: Thank them, and tell them the crack has been there since your first hundred years

effects.log: They had not known, and then they laugh. You decide the crack is a family member.

choices.text: Learn to hold the Dao so that the crack carries load

effects.log: You balance on it. A flaw that bears weight is a beam.

choices.text: Rest a hand on it until it stops hurting

effects.log: You sit with Mujin a week with your hand on the spot. Nothing changes, and it stops mattering.

events.text: A hollow in your divine foundation shows up only on feast days, when the faithful of a doorstep press too close. Your power swells and a little of you thins at the edges, like paper held to a lamp. You do not quite recognize your own voice at the end of the day.

choices.text: Sit on a doorstep during the feast, apart, and let it pass you by

effects.log: You can hear it from there. It is enough. The hollow stays quiet.

choices.text: Join the feast as a retired soldier would: stand at the back

effects.log: You stand with your sleeves folded. The press is lighter at the back, and you see the whole feast.

choices.text: Tell Mujin you thin at feasts, and ask how they hold

effects.log: Mujin says: you stand at the edge of the hall. You do.

events.text: You found a flaw in the way you hold your Dao: it leans toward everything that has a name, and away from the small things that live in it. A divine foundation can tilt for ten thousand years without cracking, and be wrong the whole time.

choices.text: Sit on a doorstep and watch what ordinary people do

effects.log: You watch an afternoon of small things: a latch, a basket, a nod. The Dao rights itself.

choices.text: Ask a retired soldier what they notice that you do not

effects.log: They say: where the dog lies. You look for dogs now.

choices.text: Let the lean stand, and tell Mujin about it

effects.log: Mujin says every general leans toward the map. You take it as a compliment and a charge.

events.text: You can feel every prayer that ever found somewhere to land in the cool quiet of your work: not as sound, but as pressure, like deep water. Today a prayer comes up through it that is more tender than most, and your qi leaps in answer before you have chosen to hear.

choices.text: Answer with a held door and a lit lamp

effects.log: The sign is small and exact. They sleep. The qi in you is quiet and old.

choices.text: Let the prayer end where it was meant to end

effects.log: You catch nothing. It lands and rests. You have made a place for it.

choices.text: Use the swell to steady a place in yourself that is tired

effects.log: You lean on it, once, in the dark. It is allowed.

events.text: A famine has driven everyone around a doorstep to your name, and the prayers are the loudest you have ever heard. Faith like that is a rare strength. It is also the strength of people who have nothing left to spend, and you know what it costs them.

choices.text: Take a little and open the soldiers' stores in dreams

effects.log: The stores open from within. You have never been so glad of an old war.

choices.text: Refuse the strength and sit at the door, as a soldier might, until relief arrives

effects.log: You wait on the step for the whole season. Relief arrives with the first frost.

choices.text: Drink it fully; you have earned this

effects.log: You take it all. The old limp in your will returns that night.

events.text: The faithful have taught you by accident. The prayer of a retired soldier, long and dull and sincere, moves your qi more than a dazzling one. It is the repetition that does it, like a sea against a rock, and you have been waiting for lightning when you should have loved the tide.

choices.text: Sit with the retired soldier's grace before a bowl of rice

effects.log: It is the same few words every day. It steadies you more than any thunder.

choices.text: Tell the pantheon the oldest prayers are the plainest

effects.log: They nod; some of them are old enough to agree.

choices.text: Keep it private; it is a god's only luxury

effects.log: You say nothing. You are glad of it.

events.text: Your people have built you a stone with no name carved on it, where everything is said. They hang offerings on its rail every dawn, not grand ones: a bowl of rice, a child's drawing of you with too many arms. The offerings do something for your qi, and something else for your temper.

choices.text: Receive the folded paper, a bowl of rice, and say thank you out loud

effects.log: You do, in the empty room. A pigeon looks up.

choices.text: Take the rice and eat it, as a guest would

effects.log: It is plain and good. The altar feels warmer.

choices.text: Ask the priest to leave the stone unadorned

effects.log: They remove the ribbons. The stone sits, wide and bare.

events.text: The keeper of a stone with no name carved on it, where everything is said has quietly become rich on your name, and the offerings now go through three hands before they reach the altar. You can feel the thinning in your qi. The priest is old, kind to their neighbours and, you think, afraid.

choices.text: Speak to the priest gently in a dream of a bare stone

effects.log: You show him the Stone with No Name. He wakes and gives his gold to the poor.

choices.text: Send an old soldier to guard the temple door

effects.log: He sits and watches. The priest steals no more.

choices.text: Ignore it; the stone does not mind

effects.log: It does not. You do, a little.

events.text: On your festival day, at a stone with no name carved on it, where everything is said, a family of strangers leaves no offering at all. They simply sit on the steps and eat, and talk, and let a child nap with her head on a worn stone. Your qi rises more from that than from the heaped altar.

choices.text: Keep the Stone with No Name quiet for their meal

effects.log: It says nothing, as it always does, and says it kindly.

choices.text: Ask the wardens to guard the family's sleeping child as a soldier would
