effects.log: They stand at the edge of the steps all night. The family never wakes.

choices.text: Study what it is to be a congregation of one meal

effects.log: You study it a season. It is the smallest rite and the whole of it.

events.text: Your domain stretches now across everything that has a name, and a small thing in it happens only because you let it: a late frost holds off, a river changes its mind. You are discovering that a god's power is mostly a list of things they decline to do.

choices.text: Decline one last thing, and write it on the Stone

effects.log: The Stone has no name for it, but takes the line. A war somewhere ends a day early.

choices.text: Reach for a small act: lift one blade from one hand

effects.log: A soldier stops mid-stroke. You never learn whom you spared.

choices.text: Walk everything that has a name and ask what is owed

effects.log: The names answer, a few at a time. You owe more than you thought, and it is a good debt.

events.text: Two of your domain's laws have begun to disagree. The same rain that feeds a field drowns a village below it, and you are the only one who can say which matters more. Mujin has offered to hold one of the laws for you while you think.

choices.text: Accept Mujin's offer to hold the law of quarrel, and think a hundred years

effects.log: Mujin holds it as a soldier holds a line. You think. The answer arrives like a ceasefire.

choices.text: Decide at once, and take the blame

effects.log: You choose and own it. The aggrieved side holds a grudge for a thousand years.

choices.text: Give the question to the people it concerns and sit by the door

effects.log: They talk all night. You sit on the step and keep the lamp lit.

events.text: A god of the throne of storms asks to see how you keep your domain. They stay a month, taking notes, asking questions, never praising. On the last day they say your domain is the least beautiful they have seen, and the most alive.

choices.text: Thank them; it is the compliment you wanted

effects.log: They go home with notes on a Stone that says nothing. They are very pleased.

choices.text: Ask what they would change in your domain of War

effects.log: They name three things. You change two, and keep the one that costs.

choices.text: Return the visit and be unpraised in their domain

effects.log: You spend a month as a guest among strangers. They hand you the good bowl.

events.text: A Revelation arrives over a doorstep the way weather arrives: not as words, but a rearrangement of the air. You spend a month deciphering it and are left with one phrase you cannot stop turning over, like a stone in the mouth. It seems to be about patience.

choices.text: Study the phrase until it opens, and then forget it

effects.log: On the last day it opens and you let it go. The Stone with No Name took it.

choices.text: Share it with the old soldiers' mess

effects.log: They think it is a drinking song and sing it. It is, somehow, correct.

choices.text: Keep it and ask no more of it

effects.log: You carry it as a soldier carries a ration: unopened, and ready.

events.text: A manual of the gods has come into your keeping, copied seven times over by seven tired hands. In the margin of the fourth chapter, someone has written in a different ink: "This does not work near the first frost." You are not sure if that is a warning or a joke.

choices.text: Try the chapter on the first frost and see why it fails

effects.log: It fails in the cold, and in failing it spells out a method.

choices.text: Ask the retired soldier whether he knows the hand

effects.log: He says it is the quartermaster of an old war. You find the quartermaster's notes.

choices.text: Add your own: "Not for the faint-hearted, nor the over-hearted"

effects.log: A line of dry soldier's wit settles in the margin.

events.text: In the night a Revelation comes that is not for you. It is meant for a young god of War, and has simply fallen on the wrong roof, here beside a doorstep. It is lovely, and it will do you a little good, and it is not yours.

choices.text: Carry it to the young god of War it was meant for, and leave before they can thank you

effects.log: They are suspicious, then moved. You eat dinner on the doorstep alone.

choices.text: Read it with a retired soldier, who says it is a fine marching song, then deliver it

effects.log: It teaches you about duty. You are late and ashamed.

choices.text: Keep it

effects.log: It does you good. You do not mention it to anyone.

events.text: A clerk of the Heavenly Court asks you to confirm a line in the Book of Fates: a retired soldier is to die in their sleep, tonight, at forty. It is a small, ordinary line. You are not required to object. The ink is not quite dry.

choices.text: Confirm it, and keep watch on his doorstep

effects.log: You sit with the retired soldier on his step at dusk. He goes in peace at the hour.

choices.text: Ask for a day, and spend it hearing his stories

effects.log: He tells you six. The sixth is the one you keep.

choices.text: Decline to confirm and say so in your own hand

effects.log: The Book rustles, and a small hesitation enters it again. He lives another winter.

events.text: You are called as a witness before a Judge of Souls. A retired soldier you once answered with a small mercy stands accused of selling short measure at a doorstep. Your testimony will not decide, but it will weigh. The Judge asks nothing but "What did you see?" and waits.

choices.text: Tell exactly what you saw at the doorstep

effects.log: You describe the bowl, the measure, the day. The Judge writes, and sighs.

choices.text: Ask whether the accused may have a quiet room to speak in first

effects.log: The Judge allows it. The truth, once said, is short.

choices.text: Decline: you leave judgment to the Stone

effects.log: The Stone has no opinion. The Judge sighs.

events.text: The Court's archivist gives you a rare gift: an hour alone with the Book of Fates, open at your own page. It is blank except for a single line in a small neat hand: "As you like." You find that this is the most comforting sentence you have read.

choices.text: Close the Book; the line is already the end of the line

effects.log: You close it. The sentence is enough for an age.

choices.text: Write a line, then rub it out, then write the first one back

effects.log: You find you prefer the first. It is a relief to have preferences.

choices.text: Ask the archivist whether the neat hand is anyone's

effects.log: The archivist says: it is the hand everyone writes in, near the end. You laugh.

events.text: You spend a century with the first frost, the nearest thing to what your Dao answers: you let it slip through your fingers, you taste it, you let it carry you. You discover that the Dao is not the element, but the way the element refuses to be held.

choices.text: Stand in the first frost and let it have your breath

effects.log: It takes what it wants. You learn cold by what it leaves.

choices.text: Pick one flake from your sleeve and let it melt on your finger

effects.log: It lasts a moment. You learn how little a thing needs to be holy.

choices.text: Ask the frost what it remembers of the summer

effects.log: It answers in a single green leaf pressed in white. You carry the leaf.

events.text: You have watched the first frost a million times, and today it looks different. It is nothing. It is the same element at a new angle. Your Dao takes a half-step and you are very careful not to move.

choices.text: Hold still while the first frost shows a new side

effects.log: The frost flowers differently on the glass. The step finishes in the cold.

choices.text: Follow the new angle out into the white

effects.log: You walk to a field where no one has been. You bring back a feather.

choices.text: Write it down plainly and leave it on the Stone

effects.log: The Stone takes it in. A sparrow reads it first.

events.text: A child at a doorstep is playing with the first frost, not knowing it. They are doing it badly and joyfully, and a thing you spent a thousand years learning falls out of their hands by accident. You are not sure whether to be annoyed.

choices.text: Watch the child scrape the first frost with a stick

effects.log: She draws a line that goes nowhere. You steal the nowhere.

choices.text: Send a warm breath to keep her fingers from the cold

effects.log: She draws on. She never knows why her hands stay warm.

choices.text: Leave her to the frost; it is her lesson

effects.log: You step back. She comes in with red cheeks and a drawing.

events.text: You are asked to give the opening address at a council of pantheons in the Stone with No Name: a short talk on what a god owes the faithful. The Will of Heaven says order, the Silent Hall says remembrance, the Green Assembly says growth, the Throne of Storms says weight. You must pick, or find a fifth.

choices.text: Say a god owes an end to the war that has not been declared

effects.log: The Throne of Storms is silent. The Will of Heaven rises.

choices.text: Say a god owes the faithful a door held open

effects.log: The Silent Hall inclines. A retired soldier in the gallery stands.

choices.text: Propose a fifth: a god owes the faithful an answer, even if it is only no

effects.log: The council is quiet a long time. Then, slowly, it nods.

events.text: A doctrine you have followed for ages turns out, on a close reading, to be a mistranslation: one word (end) was swapped by a scribe, and an entire school of devotion built on the swap. The error is beautiful. Correcting it would cost a lot of people their favourite prayer.

choices.text: Publish the correction on a plain sheet at the Stone

effects.log: The Stone takes it without comment. The reformation is long and honest.

choices.text: Footnote it, and let the old soldiers keep their word

effects.log: They keep it. They also read the footnote.

choices.text: Keep it quiet; the prayer has held ranks for ages

effects.log: You say nothing. You regret it on quiet nights.

events.text: In the Stone with No Name, a god of the Throne of Storms asks you to explain your doctrine without using any of its words. You try and fail. You try again and succeed halfway. By the end you have learned what you actually believe, which is smaller and truer than the doctrine.

choices.text: Thank them and rewrite your teaching on a single page

effects.log: It reads like a letter from a soldier. Half your students leave; the rest endure.

choices.text: Admit that the doctrine is a rank and a rank is not the army

effects.log: They smile; the Stone with No Name seems to nod.

choices.text: Defend the doctrine out of habit

effects.log: You defend it well. They go. You eat alone.

events.text: You catch yourself at the old etiquette again: keeping your sleeves folded over your hands. It is a habit from your Upper Realm centuries, and the gods in the Stone with No Name are politely baffled. A cup is just a cup here.

choices.text: Unfold your sleeves in the open, and let your hands be seen

effects.log: The Stone is unimpressed. A child, not afraid, takes your hand.

choices.text: Keep the folded sleeves; they are a soldier's habit

effects.log: A few old gods copy it. It becomes a quiet, respectful gesture.

choices.text: Study why your hands must be hidden

effects.log: You find a battle you had meant to forget. It takes a month.

events.text: You still keep a ledger of favours owed, a leftover of the immortals' exchange. The oldest line is a held door. A god would never keep one, and when a friend sees it they look briefly hurt. The ledger is accurate to the grain, and entirely beside the point.

choices.text: Hand the ledger to the retired soldier and let him decide

effects.log: He reads it and tears out one page. He gives the rest back.

choices.text: Keep it, and read it once a year at the frost

effects.log: It becomes a ritual. You grow fond of it.

choices.text: Add what you owe in the other direction, in your own words

effects.log: The sum is humbling, and the words are plain.

events.text: You flinched at a quiet room today. The Upper Realm taught you to expect a hand behind such things, and the habit lives in the shoulders long after the cause is gone. Here nothing is behind them, and your body has not yet been told.

choices.text: Sit in a quiet room on purpose and let the quiet be quiet

effects.log: Nothing happens. Your shoulders drop.

choices.text: Sit with your back to an open door and eat a bowl of rice

effects.log: Nothing comes through. The rice is good.

choices.text: Ask a god born here how they learned silence

effects.log: They say they never feared it. You envy them for an hour.

events.text: A retired soldier prays, in a doorstep, with a bowl of rice in their other hand. They do not ask for anything. They only say "thank you for the weather." You, who keep weather, find that nobody has ever thanked you for it before.

choices.text: Keep the frost off the doorstep for his morning

effects.log: He steps out, blinks at the clear stone, and sets his bowl down in the sun.

choices.text: Keep the thanks; no one has thanked a war for the weather

effects.log: It settles in you, odd and dear.

choices.text: Ask what he would change

effects.log: He says: nothing, but could the rice be warmer. You warm it.

events.text: A prayer reaches you from a retired soldier who has never believed in gods. "If you are there, I do not need you to do anything. I only wanted to say it out loud, to someone." It is the most honest prayer you have heard in a century.

choices.text: Answer nothing and sit on the doorstep with them, unseen

effects.log: You listen the whole hour. They sleep easily.

choices.text: Send a quiet sign: the porch light, lit

effects.log: They look at it a long time and do not ask.

choices.text: Ask your pantheon what this is called

effects.log: They have no word. You decide the word is "company".

events.text: A mother prays that her child's old limp might ease, and the prayer is wrong in an instructive way: she asks the wrong god, for the wrong thing, and misspells your name. It reaches you anyway, because the love in it knows the way. You stay with the wrongness of the address.

choices.text: Ease the old limp yourself and leave a warm stone by the bed

effects.log: She thanks the wrong god. The old soldier walks.

choices.text: Forward the prayer to the god of Healing with a soldier's note

effects.log: He answers with ill grace. The mother gets a remedy.

choices.text: Learn from how love finds the address through the dark

effects.log: You follow it as a sentry follows a sound. It is a map.
